title: Find a paragraph’s claims
subtitle: Separate the main assertion from its support and development.
overview: Paragraph reading begins when you can name the author’s main assertion and distinguish it from reasons, conditions, examples, and consequences.
Do not label every clause “main.” Use connective words and finite verbs to show how the paragraph develops.

sections.title: Claim map
rows: supports or explains a prior claim
draws an inference or moves to the next step

items.grc: ὁ θεὸς φῶς ἐστιν· ἐὰν δὲ ἐν τῷ φωτὶ περιπατῶμεν, κοινωνίαν ἔχομεν.
items.en: God is light; but if we walk in the light, we have fellowship.

items.grc: ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους, ὅτι ἡ ἀγάπη ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν.
items.en: Let us love one another, because love is from God.
